chapter: Tiny Bradshaw, Teddy Hill and Europe
title: Teddy Hill at the Savoy; Florida and Europe with the Cotton Club show
summary: He lived a block from the Savoy; Hill's band went to Florida in 1936 and then to London, Paris, Manchester and Dublin accompanying a Cotton Club show with Alberta Hunter and the Berry Brothers, playing the Palladium and the Moulin Rouge.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. And it was good, because as I say, at that time I lived right up on 140th Street, and I was just about a block away from the Savoy, which was very good. And that was during the time my mother was sort of ill, and that was a good thing. So I decided that I wouldn't go anywhere, you know. I just stayed home, because I could even run home between sets. You know, we played an hour. Both bands alternated an hour and -- a half hour on and a half hour off, that's what the sets were. So I could run home, you know.
But didn't you end up going to Europe?
Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes. First we made a trip to Florida in the winter, in the winter of -- what year was that? '36. Was it '36?

Yeah, I'm up to '36 now. Time flies. (Laughter). Yes, in '36. So he -- the fellow, he wanted a band from New York, so he came up and he got --so anyway, to make a long story short, so Teddy took this job in Florida, which is a good experience, you know, because I'd never been to Florida before and all the palm trees, and the first time it was during Thanksgiving we were there, and I never saw a Thanksgiving -- a Thanksgiving in the tropics was something new to me, you know. Eating the turkey dinner and whatever, and it was in the South, and I'd never spent any time in the South. You know, it was a good experience. And we came back and then he got this offer to -- we didn't get the offer as a band. I mean, you know, as just a jazz band. We got the offer as a band to accompany the show, to accompany the Cotton Club Show. It was the Cotton Club Show, which was -- and we went to Europe, you know, on that basis. And we played -- we played London, Paris, Manchester, England, Dublin, Ireland. And that was it.
Oh, this lady who's singing downtown now, Alberta Hunter.
See, she was already in London. She was living in London and she joined the show after we got there. And of course they had the Berry Brothers in the show, which

was a great dance act at that time, and different people. I can't remember who, who they were. But they had a chorus, chorus girls. They had about 12 chorus girls. It was a big show, a big production. We played the Palladium in London about -- oh, I don't know how long we played. I can't remember. Maybe we played it a month, I believe. Yeah. Then we went to Paris and we played the Moulin Rouge in Paris, and the Moulin Rouge was one of the greatest nightclubs I'd ever seen. They must have had half a dozen bands playing, and it was a great thing, you know, for me to hear all these French musicians.
Great musicians. Great musicians. The clarinet players and whatever, you know, the trumpet players. And those bands are great, fine show bands, you know.
And they had all kinds of shows. And our show was just a part of the production that was going on at the Moulin Rouge, you know, when our part of the show would come on it was --
